newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's crisis dim economic prospects - experts.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's crisis dim economic prospects - experts.

text.p: Ecuador's plans to peg the sucre currency to the dollar, the so-called "convertibility", all but collapsed with the ouster of President Abdala Bucaram, economic experts said.

The political crisis, which saw the end of Bucaram's six-month rule and Sunday's appointment as interim president of Vice President Rosalia Artega, is also bound to negatively affect the Andean nation's economic prospects for 1997, they said.
"I am pessimistic. The convertibility idea, which wasn't the best thing for the country anyway, has lost strength," former finance minister Francisco Sweet told Reuters.

He predicted that any reversal of the severe adjustment measures Bucaram wanted to introduce would disrupt fiscal accounts and push the budget deficit this year to five percent of gross domestic product, up from a projected 3.0 percent.
Sweet said inflation could exceed 50 percent or double the 1996 figure with nil economic growth.
A banker who served in the administration of former president Sixto Duran Ballen, Bucaram's predecessor, said "convertibility is a no-go."
"With this political crisis, we've squandered the work of two administrations," said the banker, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
He predicted a fiscal deficit of 7.0 percent at year-end and said the interim government, to rule until August 1998, would have no choice but to adopt populist measures.
A defiant Bucaram, who said his ouster was a disguised coup, said the new administration was condemned to failure.
"In a couple of months, everything that was achieved will be gone," he said on Sunday.
